mortal_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_001.text: At the foot of Azure Cloud, Lin Yue stood in a queue of applicants whose sleeves were cleaner than his. He was twenty-four, a kiln worker's son with a cracked thumbnail and no sensed qi. Above the recruitment terrace, cultivators crossed the mist on narrow blades. Yue watched until his neck hurt. He had spent seven years wanting to follow them and three winters learning that wanting could not lift even a grain of ash.

mortal_002.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_002.text: My name is Lin Yue. I have brought my own bedding, forty-three copper coins and a recommendation from the west kiln. I can carry clay, read a firing ledger and repair a cracked stove. I cannot sense spiritual energy. I have tried the public breath exercises every evening that work left me awake. I am asking for instruction, not a title.

mortal_003.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_003.text: Shen Qing placed a glazed testing bowl on the table. 'Hands above the rim. Let your breath stay ordinary.' Yue obeyed. The bowl remained the color of old milk. Around him, four other bowls grew pale veins of light. Qing waited through another exhalation and then removed a polished stone from beneath Yue's bowl. 'Again. This one is the blank. A proper test includes something that should not answer.'

mortal_004.speaker: narrator
mortal_004.text: Neither bowl answered. Yue tried to loosen his shoulders without making a show of it. The man behind him sighed loudly enough for everyone to hear. On the table lay admission tablets for the outer disciples, each already threaded with green cord. Qing drew a different tablet from the drawer. Its cord was plain hemp. It recorded a name, a work assignment and permission to return for another examination.

mortal_005.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_005.text: 'The first test says nothing reliable about your eventual limit. It does say we should not give you a gathering manual today.' Qing turned the hemp tablet over. 'There is a paid place on the lower terrace. You will work in the mornings. Conditioning and reading classes meet afterward. You buy ordinary meals from your wages. The examination is in eight weeks. The work continues if you fail it.'

mortal_006.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_006.text: Yue looked from the hemp cord to the green ones. He had imagined his first day ending with a sword and a robe. Instead, the mountain offered him a broom, a bed and the possibility of being told no twice. 'How many people pass after entering this way?' Qing named a number smaller than Yue hoped. Yue counted his coins again, then signed his own name.

mortal_007.speaker: narrator
mortal_007.text: The lower terrace was reached by four hundred steps. Yue climbed them with his rolled blanket, pausing twice where the rail had broken. His room held three pallets and a window facing the underside of the floating mountain. At night its stone belly shone with arrays too distant to read. He unpacked an ordinary practice sword, a borrowed primer and the jade pendant his mother had given him seven years earlier.

mortal_008.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_008.text: The jade felt warm against his palm. It always had. Yue wrapped it in cloth and put it under his bedding before opening the primer. The first page described the lower dantian as a place where a reservoir might be built. It did not say that everyone already possessed a lake of power waiting to be discovered. Beneath the printed diagram, someone had written: Learn the exit before the entrance.

mortal_009.speaker: narrator
mortal_009.text: Before dawn, a wooden clapper sounded outside. Yue carried two buckets to the communal cistern. He tried the long exhalation from the primer while climbing and nearly dropped a bucket when his vision narrowed. Water struck his sandal. He caught the handle against his knee, leaving a bruise that would trouble him all week. No hidden current rose to steady him. The remaining water still needed carrying.

mortal_010.speaker: elder_yun
mortal_010.text: Elder Yun found him breathing too quickly beside the cistern. She set the buckets down. 'You are doing three jobs badly: carrying, breathing and proving something to people who are asleep. Put the water away first. Eat before class. If the bruise changes your step, tell the supervisor.' Her eyes lingered on his name tablet. Whatever she recognized, she kept it to herself.

mortal_011.speaker: narrator
mortal_011.text: The work ledger assigned him to the ash room. Ordinary charcoal had to be sorted from spiritual furnace grit with a wet sieve. The latter could burn through a sack long after a firing ended. Yue wore thick gloves and worked slowly enough to see his mistakes. By noon, his back ached. His wages for the morning would buy two bowls of rice, a vegetable portion and a little lamp oil.

mortal_012.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_012.text: 'Sit where you can keep both feet supported,' Qing said in the practice room. 'Today we observe. No held breath, no imagined river, no drawing anything into your belly.' The lesson seemed offensively simple. Yue had spent years picturing a brilliant wheel inside himself. Now he was asked to notice when his jaw tightened. He noticed it every time another student whispered that they could feel the room.

mortal_013.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_013.text: The warmth came after thirty breaths. Yue almost raised his hand. Then he moved his fingers away from his thigh and the warmth disappeared. He wrote that down. On the next attempt his pulse seemed to travel into his thumb, but the sensation kept the same rhythm as his heart. He wrote that down too. At the bottom of the page he left the space for sensed qi empty.

mortal_014.speaker: narrator
mortal_014.text: By the fourth evening, the other workers had given his notebook a name: the Book of Nothing. Yue laughed once because it was easier than showing how much the joke hurt. Afterward he filled another page with posture, food and sleep. Those seemed too humble to belong beside cultivation diagrams. Yet the page recorded something he had never known before: he stopped noticing his breath reliably after skipping lunch.

mortal_015.speaker: elder_yun
mortal_015.text: 'An empty column is useful,' Yun told him. 'It prevents tomorrow's hope from rewriting yesterday's result.' She drew a line beneath his meal notes. 'Your body is not the enemy guarding your cultivation. It is where the work must happen. If you make it weak, the first real trace will have nowhere safe to go.' Yue did not like being advised to eat when he had asked how to become stronger.

mortal_016.speaker: narrator
mortal_016.text: The first conditioning class began with standing. Yue's thighs shook before the incense mark reached its first notch. He widened his feet to hide the tremor, and Qing tapped the outside of his knee with a wooden pointer. Three corrections later, Yue understood that the apparent stillness of a cultivator was full of small arrangements. His own arrangement collapsed whenever he thought about how he looked from the door.

mortal_017.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_017.text: Qing wrote four words on the board: Skin, Sinew, Bone, Marrow. 'Body Tempering is preparation for spiritual load. These names are assessments, not materials your body becomes. Skin means recoverable exposure. Sinew means aligned movement. Bone means supported load. Marrow means circulation sustained through work and rest. The last one is tested over a day, not during an impressive minute.'

mortal_018.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_018.text: Yue copied the words, leaving room beneath each. 'How long?' he asked. 'For you, we do not know yet,' Qing answered. 'Your first measure is eight weeks away. A stage can take a season, or longer when an injury intervenes.' Yue had saved for one season. He stared at the spaces under the words and began calculating how many morning shifts he could work without losing the afternoons.

mortal_019.speaker: narrator
mortal_019.text: On the seventh day, rain flooded the ash-room gutter. The supervisor offered an extra paid shift clearing it. The practice room would be open at the same hour. Yue's rice jar was nearly empty. His left knee still hurt when he climbed. For the first time, the choice of how to cultivate arrived without a glowing sword or a dramatic enemy. It arrived as three possible uses of an afternoon.

mortal_first_choice.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_first_choice.text: Yue laid his work token beside the primer. He could earn food, practice a careful observation lesson, or ask someone to inspect the knee he had been hiding. Each answer would leave something else waiting. He crossed out the plan to do all three before nightfall. That plan had been written by someone who did not intend to sleep.

choices.text: Take the gutter shift and buy enough food for the week.
Attend observation practice and record uncertain sensations.
Ask for a knee assessment and a lighter practice load.

mortal_work_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_work_001.text: The gutter smelled of wet ash. Yue worked with a hooked scraper while a second laborer held the basket. When his knee stiffened, he changed tasks rather than insisting on another climb. They finished after the bell. His extra coins paid for grain and a strip of dried fish. The supervisor marked the careful disposal of furnace grit beside his name. There was no mark for talent.

mortal_work_002.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_work_002.text: At supper, Yue tried to resent the absent practice hour. The fish made resentment difficult. He divided the grain into daily portions and left enough for one failed wage day. In his notebook he wrote: Worked instead of class. Then, after looking at the full jar, he added: Bought the chance to attend next week's classes without hunger.

mortal_study_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_study_001.text: The practice room was almost empty. Yue repeated the bowl exercise while Qing moved the calibrated stone without saying when. Yue called warmth three times. Only one call coincided with the stone. The other two came after he had tightened his shoulders. Qing did not award a partial success. Yue marked all three as uncertain and asked to repeat the comparison on a rested day.

mortal_study_002.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_study_002.text: He returned to a supper smaller than he wanted. Another worker sold him a portion of rice on credit, due after the next wage morning. Yue entered the debt beside the practice results. The lesson had bought clarity and cost a meal he had not yet paid for. He could see why wealthy applicants practiced more often. Knowing that did not change what his bowl had done.

mortal_recover_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_recover_001.text: The clinic assistant asked Yue to walk the length of the room before touching the knee. The bruise was ordinary, but the altered step was straining the opposite ankle. There was no spiritual wound to cleanse. Yue received a cold wrap, a reduced load and instructions to return if swelling grew. The assistant charged a small fixed fee and wrote down exactly what it covered.

mortal_recover_002.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_recover_002.text: For two days he carried half buckets. Other workers passed him on the steps. Shame moved more quickly than the pain, offering a dozen ways to prove he needed no concession. Yue used none of them. The swelling eased by the third morning. In his notebook, recovery took the space where he had wanted to put a new stage.

mortal_rejoin_001.speaker: narrator
mortal_rejoin_001.text: The next lesson began with the accounts. Every student named their available hours, ordinary expenses and recovery time. Qing made no ranking of sacrifice. One student could afford four afternoons. Another could attend one. Yue was told to build a plan he could repeat for eight weeks. For the first time, the schedule on the board looked like something that might reach the examination instead of merely promising it.

mortal_rejoin_002.speaker: shen_qing
mortal_rejoin_002.text: 'The empty bowl exercise develops control of attention,' Qing said. 'A useful practice can remain ordinary. Do not add qi to its name because that makes the work sound important.' He passed around a practice talisman bearing three strokes. The last led toward a grounding mark. 'This is release. You will copy it with ordinary ink before anyone lets you draw the admission stroke.'

mortal_rejoin_003.speaker: narrator
mortal_rejoin_003.text: Yue's first copy ended too close to the border. His second ended inside it. On the third, he drew the line slowly enough that it touched the grounding mark without thickening. Nothing shone. The ink dried brown. Qing checked the direction with a finger and gave him a fresh page. Yue had expected praise for finally succeeding. He received the next repetition.

mortal_rejoin_004.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_rejoin_004.text: At night, the pendant grew warm beneath the bedding. Yue took it out and rested it beside the practice talisman. The talisman remained dull. He moved the jade over the bowl. Nothing answered there either. Seven years ago his mother had told him to carry the pendant to Azure Cloud when he could travel safely. She had never called it a cultivation manual. He put both objects away.

mortal_rejoin_005.speaker: narrator
mortal_rejoin_005.text: Three weeks passed. His standing practice lengthened by small measures. The ash room taught his hands to recognize grain sizes through the sieve. He could finish a morning shift without folding himself over the dining table afterward. These changes disappointed the part of him that had expected light. They helped the part that now had to earn lamp oil, copy a release stroke and wake again before dawn.

mortal_rejoin_006.speaker: elder_yun
mortal_rejoin_006.text: Yun watched him rub his thumb over a newly formed callus. 'Skin assessment next week,' she said. 'It is not how much abrasion you can endure today. We need to know whether you recover, whether you can notice damage early and whether yesterday's work leaves your hands steady enough for ordinary tasks.' Yue asked if that counted as cultivation. 'It counts as preparing a cultivator who might live through the next lesson.'

mortal_rejoin_007.speaker: narrator
mortal_rejoin_007.text: For the assessment he moved a small basket of smooth stones, then a basket of coarse ones. His gloves were inspected before and after. He reported a hot spot at the base of his thumb before it split. The examiner stopped that task and asked him to copy a release stroke. His hand shook slightly. The result was recorded for comparison with the following morning.

mortal_rejoin_008.speaker: lin_yue
mortal_rejoin_008.text: Yue wanted the examiner to decide before sunset. She refused. At dawn, his hand had no new blister and the stroke was steadier. She marked Skin beside the first week of his conditioning record. The mark did not open a spiritual channel. It showed that the first load could be repeated. Yue read it five times before leaving, as if the ordinary ink might vanish when he stopped looking.
